where-am-i.label: Where Am I? pwd and ls
where-am-i.summary: Use pwd and ls together to understand your current location before touching files.

sc-pwd-purpose.title: What `pwd` tells you
sc-pwd-purpose.prompt: Which command shows the full path to your current folder?
sc-pwd-purpose.hint: Run `pwd` before interpreting a relative path, then use `ls` on the folder named in the task.

help.concept: `pwd` confirms the current directory and `ls` reports the names inside it.
help.hint_1: Run `pwd` before interpreting a relative path, then use `ls` on the folder named in the task.
help.hint_2: Do not create or move files in an inspection task; verify location and names only. The current task asks: Which command shows the full path to your current folder?

dr-safe-check-order.title: Orient before choosing an action
dr-safe-check-order.prompt: Put this safe orientation routine in order.
dr-safe-check-order.hint: Establish location first, inspect the folder second, then decide what should happen next.

help.concept: Orientation establishes context before a modifying command is chosen.
help.hint_2: Then inspect its contents before deciding what to do.

tokens.t1: Run `pwd` to confirm the current location
tokens.t2: Run `ls` to inspect the current folder
tokens.t3: Read both results before choosing the next action

pwd-current-folder.title: Know Your Current Folder
pwd-current-folder.bodyMarkdown: `pwd` prints the full path of the directory where the terminal is currently working.

ls-current-folder.title: Inspect the Current Folder
ls-current-folder.bodyMarkdown: `ls` lists the names available in the current directory so you can inspect a location before acting.
